purpose: Find publicly downloadable measured CMOS transistor I-V data at multiple temperatures between about 4 K and 300 K, to test a learned, population-shared temperature law for BSIM4 parameters (VTH0, U0, etc.) on real data.

criteria.usable_for_learned_temperature_law: at least 4 temperatures per device, several devices (different geometries or dies), Id-Vg and/or Id-Vd sweeps available as numeric files (not only plots)
priority: GF180MCU, IHP SG13G2, or another open 22-180 nm process
any CMOS process with downloadable multi-temperature data

evidence_labels.stated by the source page: taken from metadata or a landing page without reading the data
evidence_labels.stated by source code: taken from code in the source repository

criteria.download_policy: about 200 MB budget; each source in its own new directory under data/external/; files read only with python3 -I scripts stored outside those directories; pickled .npy payloads read with a restricted unpickler limited to numpy reconstruction globals

nMOS low-Vt W=4 um L=4 um, sample 3, device 136
pMOS low-Vt W=4 um L=4 um, sample 5, device 336

devices.count: 809 physical devices (n and p) on several samples/dies; 1716 non-test DC files
devices.geometries: 17 W/L pairs per polarity for low-Vt (W 0.12-4 um, L 0.04-4 um) plus W=L=1 um standard-Vt and high-Vt devices; 38 (type, Vt flavor, W, L) combinations in total; 601 devices covering all 38 combinations have data at both 4.2 K and 295 K, but only 69 of them (10 combinations: nMOS W/L 0.12/0.04, 0.12/0.05, 0.36/0.04, 1/0.04, 1/0.36, 1/1, 4/4 um; pMOS 1/0.04, 1/1, 4/4 um) have wide-sweep families (campaigns other than 2) at both temperatures

curve_types.Id-Vg: family at up to 12 Vd values (typ. Vd = 0.05 V and a set between Vg_start and 1.1 V), 111 points per curve
curve_types.Id-Vd: family at up to 11 Vg values, Vd 0 to 1.1 V, 111 points per curve
curve_types.other: diode-connected and triode Id at 11 bias points; Id at Vg=0 (leakage)
curve_types.bias_ranges: |Vg| from about 0.30-0.60 V (above threshold, depends on temperature/flavor) to 1.1 V; |Vd| 0 to 1.1 V; sweeps do not cover deep subthreshold
curve_types.note: campaign 2 files (1400 of 1716) contain only 2 Id-Vg curves and 1 Id-Vd curve over a narrow Vg range (1.05-1.1 V); campaigns 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 contain the wider families

candidates.file_format: NumPy .npy files holding one pickled Python dict each (object array). Loaded here with a restricted unpickler that allows only numpy._reconstruct, numpy.ndarray, numpy.dtype and numpy scalar; pickletools disassembly showed no other globals.
candidates.approximate_size: full record 91.3 GB (main.zip 6.18 GB, lfn_n.zip 42.0 GB, lfn_p.zip 43.2 GB); the DC folder inside main.zip is 15.9 MB uncompressed (13.3 MB compressed) and was extracted with HTTP range requests
candidates.usable_reason: Confirmed from files: 3 devices on 3 different dies (2 nMOS, 1 pMOS, all W=L=4 um) have 7 to 19 measured temperatures from 4.1 K to 295 K, which meets the >=4-temperature, several-device criterion at its minimum; geometry variation is available only at 4.2 K and 295 K (69 devices over 10 geometries with wide sweeps), so a geometry-dependent law can be fitted on two temperatures and its temperature shape checked on 3 devices.
limitations: Only 3 devices have more than 3 temperatures, and they share one geometry.
Vg sweeps start near or above threshold; subthreshold parameters (NFACTOR, VOFF) are weakly constrained.
Intermediate temperatures 4-80 K for the dense devices use smaller families (4-7 Id-Vg curves).
Campaign 2 (1400 of 1716 files, most of the 601 two-temperature devices) holds only 2 Id-Vg curves over Vg 1.05-1.1 V and 1 Id-Vd curve at Vg 1.1 V.
40-nm process differs from sky130; parameter priors from the sky130 workflow do not transfer directly.

summary: The TU Delft 40-nm CMOS dataset (4TU, CC0, doi:10.4121/c41c26f7-586f-48ca-8abe-9127b2d97c60.v1) is the only confirmed cryogenic source that meets the criterion: 3 devices (W=L=4 um, 2 nMOS on 2 dies and 1 pMOS) have 7-19 measured temperatures from 4.1 K to 295 K, and 69 devices across 10 geometries have wide-sweep 4.2 K and 295 K Id-Vg/Id-Vd families (601 devices have some data at both temperatures). The IHP SG13G2 Open PDK measurements (Apache-2.0) give 28 devices (8 LV nMOS, 8 LV pMOS, 6 HV nMOS, 6 HV pMOS, one W/L each) at 4 temperatures, but only from 233 K to 398 K. No sky130 source is usable now: the UTA campaign behind the 77 K data adds 160 K and 300 K (and one partial 100 K set) with at most 2 devices holding consistent 77/160/300 K sets, and the NIST sky130 cryogenic dataset (mds2-2997) could not be downloaded because the NIST file server timed out.
